jobs.title: Growth Marketer
jobs.description:
Growth Marketer

Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

About the Growth team

Growth Marketing at Alan covers a broad range of opportunities, including acquisition, segment and market growth, partnerships, content, experimentation, and international expansion.

We are looking for adaptable marketers who can take ownership of a defined growth problem, learn quickly, and evolve as our priorities change.

 

Your mission

As a Growth Marketer, you will independently own an ambiguous but defined Growth problem from diagnosis through execution. You will prioritise the highest-impact actions, coordinate the relevant stakeholders, and connect your work to measurable business outcomes.

Concretely, our team works on missions such as:

  • Developing our channels: scaling paid acquisition, growing visibility in AI search and LLMs like ChatGPT, or growing our strategic partnerships

  • Crafting the go-to-market strategy for our different segments (e.g. retirees, freelancers, companies,...)

  • Producing performance creatives with AI workflows to create assets at scale

Missions you could work on include:

  • Scale Alan's referral program

  • Develop and optimise our B2B and B2C growth through LinkedIn Ads

  • Own search acquisition across markets

 

What you will do

  • Independently own an ambiguous but defined Growth problem from diagnosis through execution.

  • Prioritise high-impact opportunities and make clear trade-offs.

  • Design and run experiments, campaigns, or programmes end to end.

  • Coordinate the relevant stakeholders and move initiatives forward with limited direction.

  • Use business and performance data to make decisions and establish a clear learning loop.

  • Adapt your approach based on results, customer insight, and feedback.

  • Connect your work to measurable business outcomes.

What we are looking for

  • Experience owning a meaningful Growth, acquisition, segment, market, or related Marketing scope.

  • Strong problem-framing, prioritisation, and experimentation skills.

  • Ability to make decisions based on evidence and business impact.

  • Hands-on execution combined with an understanding of adjacent teams and activities.

  • Ability to work with limited direction in an ambiguous environment.

  • Clear communication and constructive stakeholder management.

  • Curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to expand your scope over time.

  • Advanced written and verbal communication skills in English

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the B1-C1 level range.

 

🎯 Important note: we hire people, not roles.

If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply, as it can only bring learnings or success.

If you identify yourself as a woman: Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

Remember, this is just a guide, not a checklist. We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

🔖 Check out our About Alan and Career pages, as well as our Medium, blog and Glassdoor page for more info.

 

You want to know more about Alan?

  • 🙌 Perks & Benefits: Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

  • 🤘 A strong culture: People joining Alan are often surprised and delighted by our innovative working method. We have a set of cultural values that guide our approach to work

jobs.title: Technician
jobs.description:
Technician

About Enact

The next defining technological breakthrough will be in the physical world. We stand at a historical inflection point: bringing general-purpose intelligence into robotics.

At Enact we rethink the entire robotic tech stack from model architectures and data pipelines, to the actuators and sensors that feed the model. Pushing beyond pure vision and language approaches, we build a proprioceptive nerve system, and the cortex that makes sense of it, to solve dexterity through whole-body force-awareness and deploy robots for thousands of tasks in industry and beyond.

We are shaping a company where brilliant and unconventional people thrive together on solving the hardest challenges of our time. We are truth seekers. We reason from first principles, test our beliefs against reality, and trust that the best ideas can come from anyone. We move fast. We care deeply about our work and colleagues and are driven by passion to change the status quo.

If this resonates, we're excited to hear from you.

In This Role

You will work closely with our hardware team to ensure high-quality, repeatable production of our actuators and robot systems. You will help make the hardware and process better through your feedback.

  • Mechanical Assembly, Manufacturing & Build Execution: You will be responsible for the mechanical build, assembly, and manufacturing steps of our robot systems

  • Fabrication & Prototyping Support: You will help produce custom parts (fixtures, jigs, and production parts) using manufacturing machines and 3D printers and feedback ways to improve/streamline the process.

  • In-Process Quality Control: You will perform systematic in-process QC against our quality metrics and log results to keep production traceable.

  • Machine Uptime and Maintenance: You will own the upkeep of our core machines and perform routine servicing, calibration and troubleshooting.

  • You will help grow the workshop itself: improving layout, tooling, and workflows as we scale.

What We're Looking For

  • Technical Skills: Hands-on mechanical assembly, comfort with workshop tools (calipers, soldering irons, power drills), 3D printing, and basic machine operation.

  • Technical Background: A relevant trade qualification (e.g., Polymechanic, Automation Technician, Electronics Technician, or similar apprenticeship) or equivalent hands-on experience in mechanical assembly, mechatronics, or electrical systems in a professional setting.

  • Problem Solving: The ability to troubleshoot hardware issues independently and critically analyze your own work to find improvements.

  • Reads engineering drawings fluently and works independently from written instructions

  • Attention to Detail: A preference for an organized, functional workspace and a systematic approach to technical tasks.

  • Fluent in English or in German but with at least basic English skills (A2/B1) and a willingness to learn (we are an international team)

Bonus Points If You

  • Have experience in mold-making or potting/encapsulation or electric motor production

  • Are a hands-on tinkerer and have built your own robots, RC planes, or custom 3D printers, or similar in your spare time. Send us pictures or a portfolio!

  • Have CAD drawing and prototyping experience

  • Have experience with heavy duty workshop tools like lathe, mill, CNC, etc.

What we offer

  • The opportunity to make a real impact working on some of the biggest challenges of our time

  • A fast-paced learning environment alongside an outstanding, driven team

  • Ownership from day one, with the ability to iterate quickly and see your impact firsthand in an early-stage startup

  • Visa sponsorship & relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

  • A world-class in-person setup in central Zürich, with excellent prototyping, robotics, and technical infrastructure for hands-on builders

  • Competitive compensation

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Engagement
jobs.description:
Senior Manager, Engagement

About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

  • We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

  • We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

  • We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

About the Role

The way legal work gets done is changing, and Professional Services is at the centre of that transformation. We're looking for an experienced leader to run Legora's Professional Services team, building and developing the people who own our most significant professional services relationships, and setting the standard for how those firms adopt Legora and change the way they work.

This is a role for someone who has led teams through change inside large, complex organisations and knows that real transformation is designed and managed, not hoped for. You will own the performance of the team and the outcomes of the portfolio it delivers: hiring and developing Engagement Managers, setting the adoption strategy they execute against, governing quality and pace, and stepping in at the senior moments that decide whether a programme lands.

That portfolio includes our global relationship with one key Big 4 client, our most significant professional services partnership, delivered by the Engagement Managers in your team across its member firms. You will set the direction for how the firm adopts Legora worldwide, hold the programme to account, and be the senior Legora voice in the room when it matters. You will travel when needed to support your team in market and build relationships at the most senior level.

You will be critical as we continue to build a best-in-class adoption capability at Legora: designing the playbook the team works from, helping our clients realise measurable ROI, and scaling a function that can carry far more than it does today.

What You'll Do

You'll lead the Professional Services team and own the outcomes of the portfolio it delivers. Specifically, you will:

  • Lead, hire and develop the Professional Services team: set expectations, coach Engagement Managers, run performance and development conversations, and build a bench that can scale with the business.

  • Own the global adoption strategy for the portfolio, including our flagship Big 4 relationship, and hold the team accountable for coherent execution across regions and member firms.

  • Define the adoption playbook the team works from: the change-management approach, stakeholder mapping, operating cadence and target outcomes that make our programmes repeatable rather than heroic.

  • Govern delivery quality and pace: success plans, enablement, value reviews, escalation paths, and intervene where a programme is off track.

  • Act as the senior Legora relationship owner for the most important stakeholders in the portfolio, stepping in at executive moments, QBRs and escalations while your team runs the day-to-day programme.

  • Be accountable for adoption, retention and satisfaction across the portfolio, with clear measurable outcomes and ROI you can defend to clients and internally.

  • Orchestrate cross-functional engagement to accelerate client success (GTM, Product, Legal Engineering, Engineering, Marketing, Support), maintaining end-to-end context across the portfolio.

  • Partner with GTM on key commercial moments to ensure seamless transitions, continuity and exceptional customer experience, and to identify and realise expansion opportunities across the portfolio.

  • Translate customer feedback into action by collaborating closely with Product, Engineering and Marketing to inform roadmap, positioning and enablement.

  • Travel internationally to support your team on the ground and build senior relationships across member firms.

What You Bring

You care deeply about customer outcomes and you know that transformation has to be designed and led. You get satisfaction from making a team better than it was when you found it, and you're comfortable steering demanding, senior stakeholders through significant change.

We're looking for:

  • 8+ years' professional services experience - management consulting, legal, LegalTech or enterprise customer success in an AI-native B2B vertical.

  • At least 5 years in a people management role, with a track record of hiring, developing and retaining high-performing teams.

  • Extensive experience working with or inside a Big 4 firm is highly desirable — we want someone who already understands how these firms are structured, how decisions get made and how change actually lands across member firms.

  • A consulting or transformation background, with a demonstrated track record of designing and delivering change-management programmes inside large, complex organisations.

  • Experience building tailored transformation roadmaps and adoption plans and steering them to measurable outcomes — and then making that approach repeatable across a team.

  • A track record of driving adoption, retention and satisfaction with enterprise clients and senior stakeholders.

  • Strong cross-functional influence: much of what your team needs sits with Product, Engineering and GTM, and you can bring those people with you without direct authority.

  • Experience working with legal, compliance or other regulated and complex industries, or the ability to learn a complex domain exceptionally fast.

  • Strong programme and project management skills; you keep multi-workstream initiatives moving and your clients confident.

  • Excellent communication skills — written, verbal and interpersonal. You can lead boardroom conversations with legal and professional services leaders and roll up your sleeves with hands-on teams.

  • High EQ: you know when to listen, when to advise, when to act and when to let your team run.

  • A love of fast-paced, early-stage environments where you help build the playbook, not just follow it.

  • Fluency with metrics and driven by data, customer health and outcomes over process.

 

Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer

At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. We welcome people of all backgrounds and don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
Engineering Manager

ScorePlay is the AI-powered media infrastructure for sports, built to automate the content operations behind the world’s biggest sports organizations. We work with 350+ leagues, competitions, teams and broadcasters – including NBA and NFL teams, Premier League, LaLiga and Ligue 1 clubs, leading bodies like UEFA and FIBA, the Tour de France, and the Australian Open – helping them turn every moment on and off the field into high-value, structured content. Our platform brings all their media into one place and makes it effortless to find, produce and share in seconds.

Founded in 2021, we’re a 65-person team based between New York, Paris, and 10+ other countries, growing 2x year over year with 97% retention. We’ve raised $20M+ from top investors including Alexis Ohanian and Harry Stebbing’s 20VC and elite athletes like Kevin Durant, Raphaël Varane, Mario Götze, Nico Rosberg and Giannis Antetokounmpo.

If you thrive in fast-paced environments and you want to help shape how the next generation of fans experience sports, you’re in the right place. We’re on track to become the global leader in sports media, and this is definitely the best time to join our adventure.

⚙️ The role

ScorePlay is the platform major sports organizations use to manage, search and share their media, from the second it's captured to the moment it reaches everyone's screen. A photographer uploads thousands of shots after the final whistle. A live feed has to be logged and clipped into highlights while the game is still being played. The right assets have to reach 10,000+ athletes, partners and newsrooms worldwide, automatically. At 145M+ minutes of video ingested every month and 15+ petabytes stored, much of the architecture needed at that scale simply hasn't been built before.

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead one of our product engineering teams. You'll report to the Head of Engineering and sit on the engineering leadership team.

This is a technical role. You'll need a deep understanding of how our systems work to prioritize well and propose the right technical solutions. Shipping code isn't your main priority, though. Your main priorities are building the environment that lets your team ship faster, the quality of its technical decisions, the people you grow, and the problems you solve before they become incidents. Understanding how everything works is a must. Shipping code is extra.

🔥 Why this is interesting

This is a rare chance to work where engineering meets sports. You'll help build a unique, state-of-the-art product whose engineering challenges come from data volume and latency. Content has to be ingested, processed, searched and distributed at petabyte scale, often while the match is still being played. When the whistle blows, the platform has to be fast, and it has to hold.

🧠 What you'll own

People

  • Manage and grow your team: regular one-on-ones, clear expectations, direct feedback, growth plans that mean something.

  • Handle performance head-on. Recognize what's great, address what isn't early and in writing, and see it through when it doesn't improve.

  • Hire with our talent acquisition team: define the profiles your team needs, run interviews, and onboard new engineers so they ship in their first weeks.

Technical direction

  • Own the quality of your team's technical decisions: review and challenge designs, requests for comments (RFCs) and estimates.

  • Drive foundational work from problem framing to production, and balance it against client commitments.

  • Own your team's reliability: incidents, debug complex issues, postmortems, on-call health, and technical debt that gets paid down, not just listed.

Product and speed

  • Run your team's delivery with your product manager as one small team that shares context instead of handing it off.

  • Make your team faster, every quarter. Take a feature that took twelve weeks and work out how it could have taken one: cut waste, automate what can be automated, and improve your processes.

  • Define what can be delegated to AI and what needs thorough design and review, and set the guardrails that keep that line clear.

  • Push back when a product decision doesn't hold up technically, and propose what would.

  • Work with clients' technical teams on integrations and enterprise workflows when it matters.

  • Be ready to get your hands dirty and go the extra mile. Sometimes it's all hands on deck, and that means you chip in too (and ship in).

Beyond your team

  • Prioritize topics that go beyond engineering, and work with stakeholders from other teams (product, sales, customer success, support) to move them forward.

  • Contribute to engineering leadership: how we plan, how we run incidents, how we make decisions.

🛠 The stack and how we work

Golang for services. PostgreSQL, Kafka, Temporal for workflows, OpenSearch, Kubernetes, all on AWS. We use AI heavily (but wisely), in the product and in how we work as engineers.

Small cross-functional teams own their scope from conception to production. Structural decisions go through RFCs. Every week, the whole engineering team gets together to present and debate technical subjects. Every incident gets a postmortem, with real numbers attached.

🧩 What we're looking for

  • 3+ years managing engineers as an Engineering Manager, after a solid run as a backend or platform engineer. You've managed underperformance to resolution, not only coached strong performers.

  • A real technical foundation in backend and distributed systems. You don't need to write Go every day, but you can read an RFC on a search index or a Kafka topology and spot what's wrong.

  • You've led a team through a significant architectural change while still delivering for customers.

  • Initiative beyond your scope: examples of problems you owned across teams without being asked.

  • Clear written communication. At ScorePlay, decisions are made in writing.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist
jobs.description:
Senior Data Scientist

About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we are accelerating the development of oncology treatments. Today, fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs succeed in clinical trials. Clearly, new methods are needed. We combine cutting-edge biology and AI to build the next generation of insight platforms with the world's largest cohort of patient tumor avatars. These avatars fuel our AI-powered predictive engine, helping to anticipate clinical trial outcomes, validate therapies, and uncover new drug candidates.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

About the Role

Improving the quantity and quality of biological data is one of the most challenging bottlenecks to accelerate the rate of scientific discoveries in biology. In our labs at Orakl Oncology, we grow cancer cells from real patients, at scale, to generate our own experimental data. This data is deeply multi-modal and ranges from microscopic images, experimental metadata, to viability data and beyond.

We are looking for a Senior Data Scientist to own the wet-lab data chain end-to-end: from raw instrument and screening outputs through to processing pipelines. You will work on the canonical data model for lab data, as well as building the validated, analysis-ready datasets and tools our scientists and downstream teams rely on. This is a high-ownership, hands-on role at the intersection of data science, production engineering, and experimental biology. You will ship and maintain code in production, define how we model experimental data, and build the quality controls and feedback loops that let the lab catch errors early and iterate faster.

This is a role where you are expected to be in the lab, talk to scientists and lab technicians on a day-to-day basis. You will see how science is done in the lab, and then think hard about how to improve its impact. If you’re excited by complex workflows and the friction of real-life lab work, as well the power of data and AI, this position is for you.

What You'll Do

  • Own the lab-based data generation pipelines: to enable data transfer at scale from the lab to the cloud. This will involve building and improving production codebases that turn high-throughput experimental readouts into validated insights.

  • Facilitate lab operations : Maintain and/or build tools to accelerate the work of Orakl Oncology scientists.

  • Define and own the canonical data model: Design the unified data model that structures our data and is adopted across teams, ensuring data can be joined across modalities: experimental, clinical, omics, and clinical-trial event reporting.

  • Design and own data quality pipeline: Build QC that flags data quality at transfer time, and turn it into feedback loops so scientists can spot experimental errors early and integrate checks into their routine.

  • Support lab initiatives: such as automation initiatives, the development of experimental tooling to help lab scientists and technicians.

  • Drive operational efficiency: make sure that wet lab work is optimized to benefit the most from our resources (human and experimental) and ensure efficient contract and research delivery.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Masters or PhD degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Bioengineering, or a related quantitative field.

  • 3+ years of experience as a data scientist, with a proven track record of shipping and maintaining Python code in production

  • Strong hacker and tinkerer mindset. You like building things that have a real world effects.

  • Excellent proficiency in Python and SQL, and solid data-engineering skills: pipeline design and orchestration (Airflow, Dagster, dbt, or equivalent), version control (Git), testing/CI, and observability.

  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and data-storage best practices.

  • Comfortable working with noisy, real-world experimental data and directly alongside non-technical scientists.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with experimental, assay, or high-throughput screening data.

  • Working knowledge of biology, ideally in oncology, cell biology, or drug discovery.

  • Experience with image analysis / computer vision applied to microscopy data.

  • Familiarity with lab data systems / LIMS (e.g. Benchling) and experimental workflows.

Who You Are

  • Curious and autonomous: you dig into scientists' bottlenecks, connect the dots across teams, and ship without waiting for perfect specifications.

  • A fast shipper: you get working solutions into production and iterate, rather than polishing in isolation.

  • A strong communicator: you gather needs from and explain your work to non-technical scientists, acting as the data bridge across the lab and beyond.

  • At ease in a complex and interdisciplinary environment: you thrive with messy data, evolving priorities, and external constraints that come with a science-first, non-pure-tech setting.

Why Join Orakl

  • Own the wet-lab data backbone of a techbio platform from the ground up: your work directly shapes how we discover and validate cancer therapies.

  • Sit at one of the most interdisciplinary intersections in techbio: data science, production engineering, and experimental oncology, side-by-side every day.

  • High autonomy and immediately visible impact, in a fast-growing, mission-driven company backed by leading investors.

Interview Process

  1. HR Call: Getting to know each other, aligning on expectations and context.

  2. Technical Deep Dive: A deep conversation on your experience with production data pipelines, data modeling, and scientific data processing.

  3. Technical Case: A system-design and problem-solving exercise representative of the real wet-lab data challenges you'll face at Orakl.

  4. Reference Call: A conversation with one or two people you've worked with closely.

  5. Founder Interview: A final discussion with our founders on vision, culture fit, and mutual ambitions.

At Superchat, we're rebuilding how businesses talk to their customers. The phone call, the contact form, the support ticket: all of it is being replaced by messaging and AI. We're building the platform that runs underneath.

Founded in 2020, Superchat has become the platform of choice for 10,000+ businesses worldwide, from globally recognized brands like Allianz, Auto1, Enpal, Danone, and GASAG to the small businesses, dental practices, and one-person startups that need to look bigger than they are. Today, millions of messages flow through Superchat every single day.

We started as a unified inbox: one place for every channel a customer might pick, WhatsApp, email, SMS, Instagram. Then ChatGPT happened, and the second chapter began: AI agents that respond across chat, email, and voice at the quality of the best human teams.

We're 100 people, profitable, and have raised €18M in funding (last round 4.5 years ago, we've been growing on our own money since). Headquartered in Berlin.

We're hiring our first Data Engineer to own Superchat's data platform end to end, from raw product and business data to the gold tables the whole company reports on. Our engineers have already built the foundations, including a warehouse, pipelines, dbt and reverse ETL. Now we need someone to make the platform trustworthy at scale, with testing, monitoring, clear modelling layers and customer history over time. You'll set the standards for how data is modelled and documented, and work with a Business Analyst to build the gold tables that Finance, Sales, Marketing and Product rely on.

Who We Want

An experienced Data Engineer.
You bring 3+ years of building and running data pipelines in production, ideally at a SaaS company. You've owned a data platform, or a large part of one, and you're comfortable making the architecture calls yourself.

Strong in SQL and dbt.
You write and review complex SQL with ease. You've built dbt projects with layered models, tests, documentation.

At home in the Cloud.
You have worked with Data Warehouses in the Cloud, ideally AWS Redshift. BigQuery or Snowflake is also fine.

Reliability-minded.
You think in tests, freshness checks, idempotent loads and backfills. You want to know the data is wrong before a stakeholder tells you.

Curious about the business.
You want to know what MRR, churn or an "active workspace" really mean, and you model data so those definitions hold everywhere they're used. Experience with subscription billing or product usage data is a plus.

Who We Don’t Want

Pure dashboard builder.
You'd rather spend your days building dashboards and answering ad-hoc questions. That's our Business Analyst's job; yours is to build what they work from.

Pure pipeline plumber.
You move data from A to B but don't care what it means. Gold tables are only as good as the business understanding behind them.

Over-engineer.
You want Kafka, Spark and a lakehouse for data that fits comfortably in Redshift. We need pragmatic solutions that fit a 100-person company and can grow with it.

Remote-only operator.
You prefer fully remote work and don't want to build relationships in person. The data platform sits between many teams, and that works best with regular time together in our Berlin office.

Our Data Stack

  • Warehouse: AWS Redshift
  • Ingestion: Airbyte, custom Python
  • Transformation: dbt
  • Orchestration: Dagster
  • Reverse ETL: Hightouch
  • BI: Metabase

Your Day To Day

  • Own ingestion from our product database, Chargebee, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Intercom, Amplitude and other tools, using Airbyte where it works and your own Python where it doesn't.
  • Design and build the dbt models that take raw data to gold tables, with clear layers, naming and documentation that the Business Analyst and the rest of the company can rely on.
  • Run orchestration in Dagster: schedules, dependencies, freshness checks and alerting, so a stalled sync gets noticed within hours.
  • Build data quality in: dbt tests, source checks and CI on every pull request.
  • Capture history where our source systems only keep the current state, so a question like "which plan was this customer on last March?" has an answer.
  • Run the warehouse: Redshift performance and cost, access management, and AWS infrastructure in Terraform.
  • Maintain the reverse ETL syncs (Hightouch) that send data back into HubSpot, Intercom and the other tools our teams work in.

Why People Choose Us

Mission that matters. Real impact on small businesses, not abstract metrics

Funded with conviction. $18M raised and profitable

jobs.description:
Composite Technician - Airframe

About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the role

As the composite technician on the Airframe team, your core mission is to prototype carbon structures fast, in-house — from mould to finished, quality-checked part — and to bring innovative solutions that make assembly and prototyping easier. A true hands-on professional, you combine technical skills, initiative, and a maker mindset. You build tooling, lay up and finish composite parts (carbon / glass fibre), and turn the engineers' CAD into flight-worthy structures on short cycles. You are also the owner of technical drawings and supplier quotations for the parts you handle, and the one who trains production operators when a design moves to series. You thrive with minimal supervision, favour pragmatic, quick-result approaches over perfect-but-slow tooling, and are equally comfortable laying up a part, machining or printing a mould, and reading a technical drawing.

Technical skills

Key responsibilities

Rapid in-house prototyping (core)

  • Produce carbon prototype structures quickly in-house, choosing the fastest viable route rather than heavy tooling when a proto is the goal.

  • Propose innovative, simple solutions to speed up assembly and prototyping.

  • Design certain parts and prototyping tools yourself (fixtures, adapters, simple structural parts) when it is faster than going through the design loop.

  • Iterate fast with the design engineers: short loops between concept, part and feedback, flagging manufacturability issues before they cost a mould.

Tooling & moulds

  • Build and maintain moulds and tooling, in coordination with the design team; machine or 3D-print mould masters, prepare and polish mould surfaces.

  • Design and build layup jigs, trimming templates, bonding and assembly fixtures.

  • Manage the composite workshop consumables and material inventory (fabrics, resins, cores, vacuum consumables) including storage and shelf-life follow-up.

Design & documentation

  • Read and interpret 2D/3D drawings and ply books; model simple parts and tooling in CAD when needed; give manufacturability feedback early.

  • Own the technical drawings: produce and keep up to date the manufacturing drawings for the parts and tooling you handle.

  • Write and maintain clear, accessible fabrication procedures, ply books and cure logs on Confluence so processes are repeatable by others.

  • Optimise part designs for their manufacturing process: adapt geometries for plastic injection (wall thickness, draft angles, ribs) or for composite / 3D-printed fabrication (layup feasibility, demoulding, printability), in collaboration with the design engineers.

Support & improvement

  • Support assembly and mechanical testing, including preparing test coupons and samples for structural analysis.

  • Identify and propose process and quality improvements; help run the composite workshop safely (dust extraction, PPE, resin handling and waste management).

  • Own the knowledge transfer to production: train the production operators on fabrication and assembly processes, and validate that a process is repeatable by others before handover.

Candidate profile

  • Technical diploma or degree in composite materials, mechanical / aerospace manufacturing, industrial technology, or equivalent hands-on experience.

  • Proven experience in rapid in-house composite prototyping (carbon / glass fibre): hand layup, vacuum bagging, infusion and/or prepreg; mould making and surface preparation a strong plus.

  • Track record of quick, pragmatic solutions — getting a functional carbon part out fast, with sound trade-offs, rather than perfect parts requiring heavy tooling.

  • Ability to read technical drawings and ply books, and to control layup orientation, resin ratios, debulking and cure cycles with rigour and traceability.

  • Ability to produce manufacturing drawings (2D plans)

  • Understanding of design-for-manufacturing basics for plastic injection (wall thickness, draft angles) and composite / 3D-printed parts, to optimise geometries with the design engineers.

  • Hands-on finishing skills: trimming, sanding, drilling composites, structural bonding, insert fitting, and basic defect detection (porosity, delamination).

  • Proficiency with common fabrication tools (hand tools, bench equipment, 3D printer; basic machining appreciated); CAD literacy (Fusion 360, SolidWorks, FreeCAD or similar) to adapt tooling and jigs.

  • Highly autonomous — able to take ownership of tasks and drive them to completion with minimal supervision; resourceful and solution-oriented, comfortable improvising with available means.

  • Pedagogy and communication: able to write clear, accessible procedures and to train production operators so processes remain repeatable without you; rigorous on process, safety and documentation.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

Senior Computational Biologist

About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we are accelerating the development of oncology treatments. Today, fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs succeed in clinical trials. Clearly, new methods are needed. We combine cutting-edge biology and AI to build the next generation of insight platform with the world’s largest cohort of patient tumor avatars. These avatars fuel our AI-powered predictive engine, helping to anticipate clinical trial outcomes, validate therapies, and uncover new drug candidates. By generating multimodal, real-world data, we deliver insights that consistently outperform existing solutions.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalized. We collaborate with leading hospitals, research institutes and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by tier one investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

Our internal R&D programs generate a steady stream of open questions, about tumor biology, about the patient-derived models we generate across indications, and about how those models behave under drug exposure. Answering these questions takes real analytical firepower. These questions sit in different programmes across the company and run on different timelines.

What you'll do

  • You'll work alongside domain experts in cell biology, translational science, organoid establishment, drug screening, and data engineering. You will be part of the team that decides how the question gets tackled, from experimental design through interpretation.

  • Turn analyses into actionable answers that keep programme and product decisions moving, with reasoning solid enough to hold up to scrutiny.

  • Inform key programs (e.g. protocol design, commercial readiness) through deep cross analysis of molecular, functional and clinical data

  • You will communicate your results to internal and external stakeholders: publication-quality figures, panels and supporting narrative, extending to posters, presentations or manuscripts where relevant.

What we're looking for

We are looking for someone who's comfortable working on complex biological questions across different therapeutic areas and drug development programs. You will own analysis and interpretation. The ideal candidate is creative, driven, fast, rigorous and autonomous.

You will be tackling complex internal R&D subjects that are actively slowing down cancer research. Your findings will impact the field and your work is expected to reach leading scientists via international conferences and peer-reviewed papers.

Must have

  • PhD in Computational Biology, bioengineering or any related field, 2 to 3 years analyzing complex biological data in a research or biotech setting is a plus.

  • Strong experience with molecular data: You analyse omics data (transcriptomics, genomics) within the context of cell biology, translational science, organoid establishment, drug screening…

  • Interdisciplinary mindset: You quickly understand the context and framework within teams outside of your area of expertise. You are comfortable working in an interdisciplinary setting with biologists, lab-based scientists and engineers.

  • Structured communication: You communicate research findings clearly through well-documented code, notebooks, written summaries, and presentations. For example, you can highlight key figures or publications where you drove the computational biology.

  • Real interest in cancer biology: You don't need to arrive as an expert: there's considerable depth around you and you'll absorb a great deal of it. But you should find the cancer biology genuinely interesting, and be the sort of person who goes the extra mile to understand what happens behind the result.

  • Strong programming skills: Python and fluency in the scientific coding stack.

  • Fluent in English: We are an interdisciplinary and multicultural team working in English.

Nice to have

  • Strong experience working with experimentalists.

  • Comfortable holding two or three analyses in parallel without losing track of either.

  • Experience in working with or analyzing data generated from sophisticated patient-derived cellular models (e.g. PDOs, PDXOs).

  • Industry experience where your analyses fed real go/no-go decisions.

What we offer

  • Mission: work in a cutting-edge environment, on the forefront of cancer research.

  • Role: be in a high-impact research role at the core of a distinctive oncology discovery platform, where you will have access to rare PDO multi-omics and functional datasets, and a dedicated engineering counterpart to turn your methods into durable building blocks.

  • Impact: participate and have ownership in a fast-growing, multi-faceted project at the early stage of a growing start-up, with the opportunity to shape it; a role where your technical expertise will have a tangible impact on patient outcomes.

  • Team: join a collaborative, multidisciplinary team where you’ll work alongside stellar clinicians, biologists, and engineers towards a common mission.

Interview Process

  1. HR Call: Getting to know each other, aligning on expectations and context.

  2. Technical Deep Dive: A deep conversation on your experience with production data pipelines, data modeling, and scientific data processing.

  3. Technical Case: A system-design and problem-solving exercise representative of the real wet-lab data challenges you'll face at Orakl.

  4. Reference Call: A conversation with one or two people you've worked with closely.

  5. Founder Interview: A final discussion with our founders on vision, culture fit, and mutual ambitions.

Orakl Oncology is committed to diversity and equal opportunity. All qualified applications will be considered.

Role and Responsibilities

As a Senior Customer Success Manager (with Ed-tech experience), you enable AIHR's largest B2B clients to run successful learning initiatives and build a culture of learning. At AIHR, we call this role Learning Consultant rather than Customer Success Manager, because your focus goes beyond account management. You act as a strategic advisor, guiding customers in designing and implementing learning journeys that drive measurable impact.

You own a dedicated portfolio of our largest and most complex enterprise customers, from onboarding to adoption, all the way to renewal. What does that look like in practice?

  • Strategic partnership: You build strong, multi-level relationships with senior stakeholders (CHROs, VPs and Heads of HR, Heads of L&D) and make sure AIHR stays aligned with their business objectives.

  • Joint Impact Plans: You diagnose customer needs and co-create a Joint Impact Plan that connects our learning solutions to their business goals, with clear metrics to show return on investment (ROI).

  • Commercial partnership: You co-own commercial goals with our Growth Account Executives. Your deep customer knowledge shapes the renewal and expansion strategy for your accounts.

  • Team excellence: You mentor other Learning Consultants and help develop the team's best practices and playbooks.

You are successful when your clients' learners show improved work performance, not just when they complete a program, and when AIHR's impact makes them want to grow the partnership. Ultimately, your client's success is your success. Your goal is to develop their learners into T-shaped HR professionals.

On a typical day

You arrive at our beautiful office in Rotterdam or Amsterdam, grab a coffee, and after a quick chat with colleagues, you fire up your MacBook to check your calendar. You then join Jessica, our Growth Account Executive, to align on the commercial strategy for an upcoming multi-year renewal, so you show up as one team. Next, you sit down with a newer Learning Consultant to prepare a difficult conversation with one of their customers.

Before the day ends, you contribute to an internal project, sharing customer feedback about new features and improvements with the product team, including insights you summarized by feeding call transcripts into Gemini.

To wrap up the week, you join the team for a drink during our weekly activity, celebrating joint successes and getting to know new colleagues.

To set you up for success in this role, we are specifically looking for candidates with external-facing customer experience (not in-house L&D roles) and a background in education, e-learning, or ed-tech. Staff Product Designer

About Superhuman

Superhuman is an AI productivity suite that makes AI work for everyone. Over 40 million people rely on it daily to get work done. A recognized leader in productivity tools, Superhuman is the maker of popular products including Docs, Fathom, Go, GPTZero, Grammarly, and Mail. The newest product, Superhuman Go, builds on Grammarly’s ability to deliver help everywhere people work. It lets anyone build proactive agents that act as teammates across more than 1 million apps and websites, without changing how they work. Learn more at superhuman.com.

The Opportunity

At Superhuman, we're on a mission to redefine how people communicate and get work done with AI. We're hiring an experienced Staff Product Designer to join the Agents team in Berlin.

We're designing entirely new interaction patterns around how AI and humans work together through agents, through writing, from fixing your grammar to helping you schedule meetings. We're looking for someone to help us on that journey, help us build out new agents across Grammarly and Superhuman Go, and really define what these modern interaction patterns will be. You'd be involved end to end, partnering closely with our engineering and product teams, from Kyiv to Silicon Valley.

In This Role You Will:

  • Design zero to one agents. New writing and communication agents, built as AI-first products. A lot of the job is inventing interaction patterns that don't exist yet rather than applying ones that do.

  • Work with designers you'll learn from. The team spans San Francisco and Europe, with people who've come from some of the best product companies around. If you're looking for a design-focused environment with a lot of people to learn from, you'll get that here.

  • Pioneer new AI design workflows. The way we design is changing underneath us. We often start in code, refine in Figma, and ship frontend changes back into the codebase. We're defining that way of working as we go, and we want people who are excited to help build something that lets designers make whatever they can imagine.

  • Shape design strategy. Bring user insights, prototype ideas, and help build a longer-term view of where the Agents roadmap goes.

  • Lead and mentor. Raise the standard through critique, feedback, and working closely with less experienced designers.

Qualifications

  • Proficiency in industry-standard tools such as Figma and Claude Design is expected. The following outlines the skills and experience that will set exceptional candidates apart for this role.

  • Extensive experience designing complex, scalable software. The kind of tool people sit inside all day, so productivity tools, creative or CAD software, developer tools. Most of that depth lives on desktop, so mobile isn't a primary focus for this role.

  • A genuine interest in AI technology, both conceptually and in practical workflows like reading, writing and translating, and you're already experimenting with AI-driven prototyping.

  • You care about language and writing. Words are the product here, so we want someone who also thinks about how a sentence works, what makes writing sound like a person, and how tone shifts depending on who you're talking to, not just the interface around the words.

  • Comfortable working with metrics and data-driven design decision-making.

  • Bonus is having worked directly in code and shipped PRs to production.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Professional growth: We believe that autonomy and trust are key to empowering our team members to do their best, most innovative work in a way that aligns with their interests, talents, and well-being. We also support professional development and advancement with training, coaching, and regular feedback.

  • A connected team: Superhuman builds a product that helps people connect, and we apply this mindset to our own team. Our remote-first hybrid model enables a highly collaborative culture. We work to foster belonging among team members in a variety of ways. This includes our employee resource groups, Superhuman Circles, which promote connection among those with shared identities including BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ team members, women, and parents. We also celebrate our colleagues and accomplishments with global, local, and team-specific programs.

  • Comprehensive benefits for candidates based in Germany: Superhuman offers all team members competitive pay along with a benefits package encompassing life care (including mental health care and risk benefits) and ample and defined time off. We also offer support to set up a home office, wellness and pet care stipends, learning and development opportunities, and more.

  • Relocation Support: Superhuman provides comprehensive relocation support to make your move to Berlin seamless. Our package includes visa assistance, destination services to help you and your family settle in comfortably, and a relocation bonus to cover additional expenses, such as temporary housing.

We encourage you to apply

At Superhuman, we value our differences, and we encourage all to apply. Superhuman is an equal-opportunity company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race or ethnic origin, religion or belief, gender, disability, sexual identity, or age.

For more details about the personal data Superhuman collects during the recruitment process, for what purposes, and how you can address your rights, please see the Superhuman Data Privacy Notice for Candidates here.

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer (UX/UI)
jobs.description:
Senior Product Designer (UX/UI)

Optics11 is a fast-growing high-tech company based in Amsterdam, developing advanced fiber optic sensing systems for the most demanding environments. Our technology detects the earliest signs of failure in critical assets – from high-voltage energy infrastructure to subsea and defense applications – and gives our customers precise, real-time data they can act on.

The Role

As Senior Product Designer you shape how our customers and operators experience Optics11’s end-to-end underwater security solutions: from in-field sensor data acquisition, through data processing, to the software platform where that data is exposed and acted on. You combine user research with hands-on UX/UI design: you understand users in the field, turn those insights into workflows and interface designs, and hand over clear, build-ready designs to our front-end developers. You are part of the Product team in Underwater Security and work closely with Product Management, R&D, Engineering, Data Science, Software, Sales, Projects and Application Engineering.

No two weeks will look the same. You might join an Application Engineer in the field, interview operators and technicians, trace how sensor data flows from the field to the operator’s screen, prototype a new workflow in Figma, or review a front-end implementation with the developers. You own the user experience of our software platform, from research insight to interface design, and make sure real user needs guide decisions across technical, product and commercial teams.

Within your first 6–12 months, you will establish a shared, evidence-based view of our users through personas, journey maps and a structured insight repository; evolve our design system and UI guidelines for the software platform; and deliver interface designs for priority platform features that our developers can build with confidence. This reduces development risk and helps us deliver technology customers can trust in demanding, high-stakes environments

Responsibilities

  • Lead user and customer research: plan and run qualitative, quantitative and field studies across installation, operation and maintenance (for example alongside our Application Engineers), and translate findings into product and design decisions.

  • Design the user experience of our software platform: turn product requirements from Product Management and the Product Owner into information architecture, user flows and interaction patterns for complex, data-rich operator workflows (detect, assess, identify and classify), from early concepts to interactive prototypes.

  • Propose and hand over UI designs to front-end developers: create high-fidelity, build-ready designs and specifications, align on feasibility with developers and the Product Owner, and review implementations for quality and consistency.

  • Own end-to-end customer journeys: map the experience from in-field deployment and data acquisition through data processing to the software platform, including demo flows and supporting internal processes.

  • Manage personas and customer insights: maintain the persona set and a central research repository, and synthesise learnings collected across the organisation.

  • Validate and measure outcomes: run usability tests before and after release, define adoption and usability metrics, and report impact to stakeholders.

  • Evolve and maintain our design system: extend the existing basis with UI components, patterns and guidelines that keep the platform consistent, accessible and efficient to develop.

  • Partner across the organisation: work closely with Product Management, Product Ownership and System Architecture, as well as Sales, Business Development, Application Engineering, Support and Marketing, to prioritise development, reduce product risk and advance user-centred practices.


Requirements

  • Master’s degree in interaction design, human-computer interaction, computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

  • 5+ years of experience in UX or product design, covering both user research and hands-on UX/UI design, preferably in defense or other technical, high-stakes industries.

  • A portfolio showing end-to-end work, from research and workflows to high-fidelity UX/UI for data-rich professional software (e.g. situational-awareness, control-room or analytics applications).

  • Experience working on integrated software platforms rather than isolated websites or prototypes.

  • Experience handing designs over to front-end developers and working with and evolving a design system, with a working understanding of front-end technology and its constraints.

  • Proficiency in qualitative and quantitative research methods, with the ability to translate data into actionable insights and design proposals.

  • Understanding of end-to-end systems in which sensor data is acquired in the field, processed and exposed on a software platform, ideally in complex or regulated environments.

  • Able to translate complex technical workflows and data into clear, intuitive interfaces, with strong attention to visual detail, consistency and quality.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; able to present research and designs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Proficiency in Figma and in research and collaboration tools such as Jira Product Discovery, Dovetail and Miro.

  • Willingness to travel and do field research.

  • Driver’s license B (or international equivalent).

  • Ability to pass a background / security screening by the Dutch AIVD/MIVD, as you will be working with clients in the defense industry.

Nice to Have

  • Big plus: Experience with underwater acoustics or sonar software.

  • Plus: Experience in design leadership, or in setting up design practices in a growing organisation.

  • Plus: Front-end skills (e.g. HTML/CSS, React) for prototyping next to AI based tooling.

  • Plus: Proficiency in Dutch.


Screening

You will work with clients in the defense and security sectors. Obtaining a Certificate of No Objection issued by the AIVD, the Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service, is mandatory. This means you will need to undergo a security screening. We will explain the process and guide you through the applicable requirements.

The Director will also lead the reorganization of support into two specialized teams: Tier 1 for the inbound queue and live calls, and Tier 2 for deeper, project-managed work, including root-cause resolution of chronic hardware issues. The team focuses on hardware support, and its work directly influences product uptime in the field.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy and Team Leadership

  • Lead the Tier 1 and Tier 2 support teams through the reorganization.
  • Create clear performance standards and hold teams accountable to them through regular quality reviews and coaching.
  • Build performance metrics and frameworks for individuals and teams. Co-own the annual operating plan and headcount planning.
  • Set annual and quarterly support goals that cascade into team and individual objectives, and review progress with the executive team each quarter.
  • Define the team operating model, including span of control, shift coverage, and staffing levels, and update it as volume and product lines grow.
  • Run a leadership development program for Team Leads and Managers covering coaching, decision-making, and cross-functional communication.

Operations, Quality, and Hardware Outcomes

  • Own support quality and customer effort. Reduce repeat contacts and ticket volume per device or account.
  • Lead escalations for Sev 1 incidents and strategic accounts and hold executive incident reviews.
  • Maintain visibility into at-risk tickets, outages, and field hardware or sensor failures, and act on early warnings before customers escalate.
  • Reduce recurring hardware issues by leading root-cause investigations with hardware, engineering, and field teams.
  • Design processes, playbooks, and SOPs. Keep the knowledge base current and ramp new hires to full productivity within 30 days.
  • Evolve the support tech stack (ticketing, knowledge base, remote diagnostics) and integrate it with CS, sales, and product systems, sequenced against the product roadmap.

AI, Product, and Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Lead AI integration: 100% tool adoption and 20%+ agent productivity gain within 18 months. Champion triage, diagnostics, self-service, and agent-assist tools.
  • Serve as the primary liaison between support and Product and Engineering, turning frontline insights and recurring issues into reliability roadmap priorities.
  • Present quarterly support health metrics to executives, with monthly ticket trend data and recommended actions.
  • Partner with Customer Success, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Operations on handoffs and at-risk account signals.
  • Lead support strategy for Mexico and Latin America, including localized language support and follow-the-sun coverage. Maintain 100% compliance with local labor and data privacy rules.

Qualifications

  • Experience: 8+ years in customer or technical support, including B2B SaaS or hardware-enabled SaaS. 4+ years in director-level leadership managing 15+ people across multiple supervisory levels. 2+ years directly accountable for SLA, CSAT, or quality metrics.
  • Industry: 3+ years in SaaS, HaaS, IoT, predictive maintenance, manufacturing, or similar technical B2B sectors strongly preferred. Understanding of incident management and hardware or software troubleshooting in connected devices.
  • Leadership: Proven track record building high-performing support organizations, recruiting, developing leaders, and creating accountability.
  • Strategic execution: Measurable gains in CSAT, SLA compliance, resolution time, and first contact resolution.
  • Global experience: 2+ years leading remote, shift-based, or follow-the-sun teams. Mexico or Latin America experience highly valued.
  • Technical and AI fluency: Comfort with diagnostics, data analytics, and AI in support workflows.
  • Operations orientation: Strong background in well-structured operations and running processes that handle incoming work reliably.
  • Hardware or technical background: Preferred, not required. Ability to translate field data into technical discussions with engineering.
  • Comfort with ambiguity: Experience building new structures while keeping operations stable.
  • Proactive support or implementation experience: A plus.

Desired Skills and Attributes

  • Executive presence with C-suite audiences, especially during severe incidents.
  • Data-driven, with the ability to turn metrics into operational decisions.
  • A change agent who thrives under pressure and actively improves processes.
  • A talent developer who builds advancement paths.
  • Understands manufacturing operations, IoT sensors, and asset-intensive industries.
  • Collaborative, influencing across Product, Engineering, and Customer Success without direct authority.
  • Results-oriented, with high ethical standards.

jobs.title: Head of Strategic Pursuits
jobs.description:
Head of Strategic Pursuits

About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

ElevenLabs is looking for a Head of Strategic Pursuits to lead our largest, most complex and most transformational enterprise deals around the world, from first executive conversation through signature and into deployment.

This is a global leadership role reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer. Strategic Pursuits is not traditional sales support. It is a specialized deal leadership function that partners with Account Executives to win opportunities that require significantly more executive engagement, creativity, and cross-functional coordination than a standard sales cycle. These are the deals that don't fit the playbook. They are structured in new ways, they involve multiple senior stakeholders on the customer side (and sometimes their boards and investors), and they pull in nearly every function at ElevenLabs to get done.

You will own the pursuit strategy for these opportunities. That means shaping the transformation narrative with the customer's C-suite, building the business case, designing the solution and the commercial model, running the negotiation, and bringing Sales, Product, Engineering, FDE, Finance, Legal, Partners, and our own executives together to move the deal forward and clear what's in the way. The AE continues to own the account and the relationship. Your job is to make sure we win the deal and that it's structured to set us and the customer up for long-term success.

The work doesn't stop at one deal. You will turn what we learn from each strategic pursuit into repeatable motions: playbooks the field can reuse, input into how we price and package, signal to Product on what our largest customers need, and clean handoffs into deployment so what we sold is what gets delivered.

This is not a sales operations, deal desk, or program management role, and it is not a quota-carrying territory role. We are looking for someone who has personally led and structured nine-figure-scale, multi-year enterprise deals, is comfortable going well outside the playbook to get them done, and has the executive presence to sit across from a Fortune 500 CEO. While initially a senior IC role, there is the potential to build out a team under this function.

In this role you will

  • Lead strategic deals. Own the pursuit strategy for our largest and most complex enterprise opportunities, partnering with account teams from qualification through close. Help decide which pursuits warrant this level of investment and where your time goes.

  • Build executive engagement. Develop C-suite relationships at our most important customers and prospects, shape transformation narratives, and create compelling business cases tied to measurable outcomes. Bring in the CRO, CEO, and other ElevenLabs executives at the right moments with a clear role for each.

  • Orchestrate cross-functional execution. Bring together Sales, Product, Engineering, FDE, Finance, Legal, Partners, and executive sponsors to accelerate deal progression and remove blockers. Run the pursuit like a program, with a clear plan, owners, and a cadence, without becoming the bottleneck.

  • Structure and win complex transactions. Drive competitive strategy, solution design, commercial models, negotiations, and creative deal structures (multi-year commitments, partnerships, co-development, platform and marketplace models, and others we haven't invented yet) to secure transformational agreements that are good for the customer and for ElevenLabs.

  • Work across senior stakeholders on both sides. Navigate complex buying committees, procurement, legal, and in some cases boards and investors, and keep the deal moving when it gets stuck at the top.

  • Partner on global and strategic accounts. Work closely with regional leaders and account teams on our most important global accounts, bringing a consistent strategy across regions and product lines.

  • Build repeatable winning motions. Turn strategic deals into scalable playbooks, improve pricing and packaging, influence product priorities with evidence from the largest deals in the market, and ensure successful handoffs into deployment.

  • Raise the bar on deal craft across the org. Coach AEs and regional leaders on executive selling, business case development, and deal structuring so the whole Revenue organization gets better at winning big.

  • Be the CRO's partner on big bets. Bring a clear point of view on which deals to pursue, how to structure them, and when to walk away, and represent that view in leadership and executive forums.

Requirements

  • 15+ years of relevant experience in enterprise sales, strategic deals, or business development at technology companies, with a track record of leading and closing very large, complex, multi-year transactions.

  • Deep deal structuring experience. You have personally designed and negotiated creative commercial structures and know how to make the economics work for both sides while protecting the business.

  • Executive presence. You are credible with C-suite executives at the largest enterprises in the world and can hold the room alongside our CRO and CEO.

  • Comfort outside the playbook. You thrive in deals that don't follow a standard process, and you know when to break the playbook and when to rely on it.

  • Cross-functional orchestration. You can rally Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal, and executives around a deal when none of them report to you, and you do it by being prepared, decisive, and easy to work with.

  • Business case and value fluency. You can build a credible, quantified business case tied to customer outcomes and defend it to a CFO.

  • Strong commercial judgment. You understand pricing, margin, and long-term account economics, and you know the difference between a big deal and a good deal.

  • Technical fluency. You understand AI and platform products well enough to shape solution design and hold your own with a customer's CTO.

  • Operator mentality. You care about what happens after signature, and you make sure what we sold gets deployed successfully.

  • Ability to operate globally. You are comfortable leading pursuits with teams and customers across AMER, EMEA, APAC, LATAM, and India.

  • Willingness to travel. Must be willing and able to travel up to 40% of the time, often with customers' and ElevenLabs' executives.

Bonus points

  • Experience building or leading a strategic pursuits, strategic deals, or global accounts function at a high-growth AI, cloud, or enterprise software company.

  • Experience selling AI, voice, conversational AI, or platform/API products to large enterprises.

  • Experience structuring partnerships, marketplace, or co-sell agreements alongside direct deals.

  • Experience in a company where the product and the market move weekly and deals have to keep up.

Location

This is a remote global role within the Revenue organization. You will travel up to 50% for

customer and executive meetings and for working sessions with regional sales leadership.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.
